STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel is a white square flat plate. It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall, so it is a flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-large, around 25-27 cm.
b) Reference cue: the cherry tomato (3 cm) on the left is about 1 cm-scale relative to the plate. The plate spans roughly 8-9 cherry tomato lengths along its visible width (about 450 px for a plate of roughly 25 cm). Count gives about 24-27 cm.
Reconciled width: about 26 cm, so area = 26 x 26 = 676 cm2.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Wheat berries / farro-style grain (base with greens and vegetables): covers roughly 20% of the plate, footprint about 135 cm2. Mound of grain, peak about 2 cm, average about 1 cm thick (mound averages half its peak; a few grains high at centre). Volume = 135 x 1.0 = 135 ml. Bulk density cooked grain 0.8: 135 x 0.8 = about 108 g.
- Yellow squash slices and onion: about 6% of plate, about 40 cm2, chopped vegetable layer about 1 cm thick: 40 ml x 0.6 = about 24 g.
- Cooked leafy greens (spinach/chard strands): small amount, about 10 g.
- Cherry tomatoes: 2 whole visible (one left, one near bottom) plus 1 partly hidden under the grain pile: 3 x 15 g = 45 g.
- Olive oil / light sauce smear: about 5 g.

Total: 108 + 24 + 10 + 45 + 5 = about 192 g.

Energy per 100 g (cooked):
- Cooked grain (wheat berries/farro): about 340 kcal per 100 g dry basis, about 130 kcal per 100 g cooked; use 130 for cooked grain.
- Squash/onion vegetables: about 25 kcal per 100 g.
- Cooked leafy greens: about 25 kcal per 100 g.
- Cherry tomatoes: about 18 kcal per 100 g.
- Olive oil sauce: about 880 kcal per 100 g.

Estimated total energy: 108 x 1.30 = 140 kcal; squash 24 x 0.25 = 6; greens 10 x 0.25 = 3; tomatoes 45 x 0.18 = 8; oil 5 x 8.8 = 44. Total about 200 kcal.
